target_customer: Job seekers, mainly students, with planned premium features and employer matching
problem: Resumes were static documents that were hard to restyle, tailor per employer and share online.
business_model: Freemium; premium features such as custom domains were planned

founders.name: Dane Hurtubise
previous_startups: Parklet (acquired by Greenhouse, after JobSpice per YC bio)

founders.name: Andrew McCollum
founders.background_notes: Launch coverage calls him a Facebook co-founder and its original designer.

competitors.name: Monster
competitors.what: Established online job board with resume posting

competitors.name: VisualCV
competitors.what: Web based resume and profile page
competitors.funding_then: Reported funding from February 2008 per CB Insights; amount unverified

technical_complexity.rationale: CSS themed resume pages with PDF export; mostly design and standard web work.

defensibility.rationale: Templates and hosting were easy to copy and the market had many resume tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source reports action against JobSpice; AlternativeTo marks it discontinued.

market_need_then: Students and job seekers paid over $100 for resume services per launch coverage; no usage figures found.

branding.community_and_virality: Press attention came largely from McCollum's Facebook background, not from the JobSpice brand.

brand_strength.rationale: No source describes the brand beyond the name and a short YC profile, so no evidence of brand pull was found.

outcome_analysis: JobSpice launched in August 2009 to modest press interest centered on a Facebook co-founder, with no funding disclosed. It is listed inactive and marked discontinued by AlternativeTo, but no shutdown notice or reason was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: jobspice.com did not resolve, treated as a dead site, not worked around. YC lists both founders as CEO. Education not found. CB Insights VisualCV funding was in a snippet only.
